documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of note: 03:40, HD1
Pt is a 68-year-old female presenting from home via EMS with fever, chills, and dysuria.
CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever and burning with urination x 2 days.
HPI:
Two days of urinary frequency, dysuria, and suprapubic discomfort. Yesterday evening developed rigors and flank ache on the right.
Daughter called EMS after pt felt weak standing from a chair. No chest pain. No vomiting.
No recent instrumentation, no indwelling catheter, no stones known.
Arrived 02:10. Temperature 39.4 C at triage, HR 118, BP 88/50, respiratory rate 30, SpO2 88% on RA.
Placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%. Denies dyspnea at rest but reports feeling winded.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Hypertension.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, last A1c 7.4 percent per outside records.
Recurrent urinary tract infections, 2 episodes in the past 18 months.
Osteoarthritis of both knees.
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
Cholecystectomy. Right total knee arthroplasty.
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg BID
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg PRN
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash.
SOCIAL: lives with daughter, independent with ADLs, walks with a cane outdoors. Never smoked. No alcohol.
FAMILY HISTORY: mother with CVA, father with CAD.
ROS: Positive for fever, chills, dysuria, right flank pain, fatigue. Negative for cough, sore throat, diarrhea, rash, calf pain.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Gen: ill-appearing, diaphoretic, cooperative and answering questions appropriately.
HEENT: mucous membranes dry, sclerae anicteric.
Neck: supple, no JVD.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Extremities warm early, then cool with capillary refill 3 sec.
Pulm: tachypneic, accessory muscle use mild, lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abd: soft, suprapubic tenderness, right CVA tenderness on percussion. No rebound.
Skin: no rash, no ulcers, no lines.
Neuro: no focal deficit, moves all extremities, follows commands.
LABS / STUDIES:
WBC 21,300 with 14% bands. Hgb 11.8, platelets 84,000.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL). BUN 38. Na 133, K 4.6, HCO3 19.
Total bili 1.4, AST 32, ALT 28. INR 1.2.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field, nitrite positive, many bacteria.
Blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
CXR portable: no consolidation, no effusion.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic changes.
ASSESSMENT:
68-year-old female with septic shock, source presumed urinary, with AKI and thrombocytopenia.
PLAN:
Sepsis - Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61. Continue normal saline at 100 mL/hr.
Antibiotic: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added pending culture data.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 micrograms/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 micrograms/kg/min to keep MAP above 65. Central line placed R IJ.
AKI - hold lisinopril and metformin, avoid NSAIDs, monitor urine output hourly with Foley, trend creatinine.
Thrombocytopenia - likely sepsis related, daily CBC, no heparin flushes beyond line protocol, no signs of bleeding.
Hypoxemia - continue 6L NC, wean for SpO2 above 92 percent, incentive spirometry.
Glycemic control - SSI per protocol, q4h glucose checks.
Disposition - ICU. Discussed with daughter at bedside. Attending notified and at bedside for line placement.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: ICU PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:15
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports feeling less shaky overnight. Dysuria improved. No chest pain, no nausea. Slept in short intervals.
Nursing reports urine output 22 mL/hr overnight, now 35 mL/hr.
OVERNIGHT EVENTS:
Norepinephrine requirement peaked at 0.12 micrograms/kg/min at 05:30, now down to 0.06 micrograms/kg/min.
MAP maintained above 65 since 05:00. BP at 06:40 was 104/58.
Weaned to 4L NC, SpO2 94 percent.
Additional 500 mL normal saline given at 03:20 for MAP 62.
EXAM:
Gen: less diaphoretic, no distress.
Cardiac: tachycardic, no murmur. Right IJ site clean and dry.
Pulm: breath sounds clear, no crackles.
Abd: mild suprapubic tenderness, right CVA tenderness improved.
Ext: warm, no edema, no petechiae.
LABS:
WBC 17,800, platelets 91,000, Hgb 11.2.
Creatinine 2.3 mg/dL, BUN 41, K 4.2, HCO3 21.
Culture: blood culture x2 and urine culture still pending as of this morning; gram stain of urine with gram negative rods.
ASSESSMENT / PLAN:
Septic shock, urinary source - improving hemodynamically. Wean norepinephrine for MAP above 65, goal off today.
Antibiotic: continue piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h (renally adjusted) and vancomycin by trough-guided dosing.
AKI - creatinine trending down, continue strict I/O, hold ACE inhibitor and metformin.
Thrombocytopenia - platelets rising, no transfusion, recheck AM.
Hypoxemia - continue wean of supplemental O2, ambulate with assist when off pressors.
Lines - reassess need for central line once vasopressor off.
Daughter updated at 07:00.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD5, 08:05, step-down unit
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt ambulated to hallway and back twice yesterday with walker and one assist. Appetite returning, ate most of breakfast.
No fever since HD3. Denies dysuria. Reports mild right flank soreness only with palpation.
INTERVAL EVENTS:
Norepinephrine off since HD2 at 19:40; no recurrence of hypotension. Central line removed HD4.
Off supplemental oxygen since HD3, SpO2 95 percent on room air, respiratory rate documented at 18 this morning.
Foley removed HD4, voiding spontaneously, urine output 1.6 L over 24 hours.
Culture: blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; urine culture with E. coli greater than 100,000 CFU/mL, pan-sensitive except ampicillin.
Vancomycin discontinued HD3 after gram negative organism identified. Remained on IV antibiotics through day 3, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID per sensitivities.
EXAM:
Gen: comfortable, sitting up in chair.
Cardiac: regular rate, no murmur. BP this morning 122/70.
Pulm: clear bilaterally, good effort.
Abd: soft, nontender, no suprapubic tenderness.
Ext: no edema, no rash, no line sites.
LABS:
WBC 8,900, no bands reported. Platelets 188,000. Hgb 10.6.
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, BUN 18, K 4.0, HCO3 24.
ASSESSMENT / PLAN:
Sepsis from E. coli pyelonephritis with bacteremia - clinically resolved, afebrile, on appropriate oral therapy.
Continue oral ciprofloxacin to complete 14-day total course from first dose.
AKI - nearly resolved, resume lisinopril at 10 mg daily today and recheck creatinine in the morning. Metformin to resume after creatinine confirmed stable.
Thrombocytopenia - resolved, no further CBC monitoring needed beyond AM labs.
Mobility - PT following, continue ambulation TID.
Anticipate discharge home with daughter tomorrow if labs stable.
Attending rounded at bedside 08:40 and agrees with plan.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: 6 days, discharged HD6 at 14:20.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Sepsis secondary to E. coli pyelonephritis with bacteremia
2. Acute kidney injury, resolved
3. Sepsis-associated thrombocytopenia, resolved
4. Hypertension
5. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
HOSPITAL COURSE:
68-year-old female arrived 02:10 on HD1 with 2 days of dysuria and flank pain followed by rigors and weakness.
Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.

Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 micrograms/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 micrograms/kg/min to keep MAP above 65; weaned off HD2 at 19:40.
Antibiotic: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Vancomycin stopped HD3 once E. coli identified. Narrowed to oral ciprofloxacin per sensitivities.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 on admission. Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL and platelets 214,000 on day of discharge.
Oxygen weaned to room air HD3. Foley and central line removed HD4. Afebrile since HD3.
PT cleared pt for home with walker; ambulating 200 feet with one assist.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID to complete course, last dose per instruction sheet
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg BID, resumed HD6
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg PRN pain
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Drink at least 6-8 glasses of water daily. Finish all antibiotic doses.
Return for fever above 38.0 C, shaking chills, flank pain, vomiting, decreased urination, or lightheadedness.
No NSAIDs.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days for repeat BMP and CBC.
Urology referral placed for recurrent urinary tract infections.
Discharged home with daughter, who verbalized understanding of instructions and medication list.
